fixtures.role: Unmodified upstream fixture: one comma-separated row of 1200 doubles, a mixture of a Gumbel and a Gaussian component, used by the MLE section of GumbelDistributionFitter_test.cpp with unit weights and the initial guess (4.0, 2.0).

source_anchors.operation: The default initial guess is init_param_(0.06, 3.0, 0.5); the first class-test fit case uses it and converges from x0 = 3.0 to x0 = 0.3
Residual A * exp(-(x - x0) * (x - x0) / sig2) - y with sig2 = 2 * sig * sig hoisted out of the loop
Centre derivative written as A * j0 * (-(-2 * x + 2.0 * x0) / sig2), a double negation kept verbatim
Eigen::LevenbergMarquardt<GaussFunctor> with default Parameters: factor 100, maxfev 400, ftol = xtol = sqrt(eps), gtol 0
Throws UnableToFit only for ImproperInputParameters (0) and TooManyFunctionEvaluation (5); the source comment records that every other state is a good termination
x_init(2) = fabs(x_init(2)); the comment says a negative sigma is reachable and |sigma| is the correct solution
int0 = A / pdf(ndf, x0) with the comment that multiplying the CDF by A is wrong; both eval overloads use this two-step normalization
log_eval_no_normalize = -log(sigma) - halflogtwopi - 0.5 * pow((x - x0) / sigma, 2.0); no guard on a non-positive sigma
Class documentation promises getGnuplotFormula(); no such member exists on this class
halflogtwopi is a private non-static data member with an initializer, so every GaussFitResult carries its own copy of the constant
@note: the fitted function is a customized gamma distribution that is 0.0 when b or p is <= 0, so an unconstrained optimizer can be used
The default initial guess is init_param_(1.0, 5.0); the class test overrides it with (1.0, 3.0)
Residual branches on b > 0.0 && p > 0.0; otherwise every residual is -y, the customized density's zero branch
Jacobian branches the same way and is set to all zeros outside the positive quadrant
Shape derivative uses boost::math::digamma(p) and tgamma(p) twice, once squared through std::pow(tgamma(p), 2)
Throws UnableToFit for status <= ImproperInputParameters; after a completed minimize only ImproperInputParameters is reachable
GumbelDistributionFitResult::eval is declared and defined nowhere in the SDK; any C++ caller fails to link
GumbelDistributionFitter::fitWeighted is declared with a full Doxygen block including @exception and defined nowhere; the class test uses GumbelMaxLikelihoodFitter instead
The constructor assigns GumbelDistributionFitResult(0.25, 0.1) over the default-constructed member, so the fitter's guess is not the result type's default (1.0, 2.0)
Residual forms z = exp((a - x) / b) first, then (z * exp(-z)) / b - y
Analytic Jacobian; no fabs is applied to the scale, so fit can report a negative b
Throws UnableToFit for status <= ImproperInputParameters
Functor<double>(2, 2): two residuals for a one-dimensional objective, because Eigen rejects values() < inputs()
sigma = fabs(x(1)): the scale enters through its absolute value so the search stays unconstrained
The weight iterator is advanced in lockstep with the sample iterator and the two sizes are never compared; a short weight vector is read past its end

Running sum of w * (-logsigma - diff - exp(-diff)) in index order, negated once at the end into fvec(0); fvec(1) stays 0, so Levenberg-Marquardt minimizes the square of the weighted negative log-likelihood
Eigen::NumericalDiff wraps the functor: the Jacobian is a forward difference at step sqrt(eps) * |x_j|, and its n + 1 evaluations are charged against maxfev
Throws UnableToFit for status <= ImproperInputParameters
init_param_ is overwritten with the fit result, so a second fitWeighted continues from the first; the returned scale is fabs(x_init(1))
The default initial guess is init_param_({0.25, 0.1}); with no samples the objective is identically zero, the gradient vanishes and the solver returns the guess unchanged
Published case-one parameters A = 1.01898275662372, x0 = 0.300612870901173, sigma = 0.136316330927453 at the default tolerance
Published case-two parameters A = 175011.893006749, x0 = 240.1007246725147, sigma = 0.00046642320683761701, the case the source comment says needs fabs
Published static eval intensities at the seven m/z values of the initial guess
TOLERANCE_ABSOLUTE(0.01), expected b = 7.25 and p = 3.11
TOLERANCE_ABSOLUTE(0.1) set here and still in force for the MLE section at line 154, since ClassTest tolerances persist for the rest of the file
fitWeighted({}, {}) is asserted to return the initial parameters; three sections depend on the empty-input path

evidence: Tier 3 source review for every parameter value: the expected numbers are transcribed from the four _test.cpp files, which are the only oracle available without building C++. Tier 4 independent checks that depend on no transcribed literal: the maximum-likelihood result is verified to be a local minimum of the source's own weighted negative log-likelihood by recomputing it at the fit and at eight neighbours, with the objective strictly positive (1310.76) so that minimizing its square is minimizing it; the solver is driven onto a zero-residual linear problem with the exact solution y = 1 + 2x; the four Blue's-algorithm constants are asserted against 2.0f64.powi(e) (this caught two wrong literals); both norms are exercised at 1e200 and 1e-200; digamma is checked against psi(1) = -gamma, psi(1/2) = -gamma - 2 ln 2 and the recurrence at eleven integer points; and each density is checked against its closed-form mode and symmetry. No tier 1 or tier 2 evidence exists: no retained C++ output exists for a MATH/STATISTICS fitter and no oracle driver was built. Cross-check: an independent Python transcription of the same algorithm, on a different platform and libm, reaches the identical f64 values 0.5015861406501456, 0.9955965893616037 and (2.001561295066307, 0.6230114376387215) for the three Gumbel cases.

achieved_agreement.cpp_tolerance: TOLERANCE_ABSOLUTE(0.1), inherited from the fit section above

achieved_agreement.case: GumbelMaxLikelihoodFitter on the synthetic grid (a, b)

class_test_sections.note: Every START_SECTION of the four _test.cpp files has a named Rust test and one concrete reproduced value; the per-section table is in docs/DISTRIBUTION_FITTERS_SUPPORT.md section 6.

cpp_issues: GumbelDistributionFitter.h:51 declares GumbelDistributionFitResult::eval and no definition exists anywhere in the SDK; a C++ caller fails to link.
GumbelDistributionFitter.h:81 declares fitWeighted, with a full Doxygen block, and no definition exists; the class test reaches a weighted fit through GumbelMaxLikelihoodFitter instead.
GaussFitter.h:30, GumbelDistributionFitter.h:28-29 and GumbelMaxLikelihoodFitter.h:26-27 all document a getGnuplotFormula() member that none of the three classes has.
GumbelMaxLikelihoodFitter.cpp:58-63 advances a weight iterator in lockstep with the sample iterator without comparing the two sizes, reading past the end of a short weight vector.

GumbelMaxLikelihoodFitter.cpp:62-66 places the weighted negative log-likelihood in fvec(0) of a two-element residual vector, so Levenberg-Marquardt minimizes its square. On data where the objective stays strictly positive this is the maximum-likelihood estimate, verified independently here; where the objective can reach zero the iteration is attracted to that contour instead.
gaps: No tier-1 differential evidence: no retained C++ output exists for these fitters and no oracle driver linking the prebuilt libOpenMS was built.

digamma is the recurrence plus the asymptotic series through B14, not Boost's rational minimax approximation; agreement is better than 1e-14 absolute against closed forms and the value enters only the Jacobian.
tgamma comes from the already-vendored libm crate rather than the platform's std::tgamma; both are accurate to about one unit in the last place.

Eigen may vectorize the inner sums of its norms and dot products, which this port accumulates sequentially; the difference is at most one unit in the last place per reduction and is the likely origin of the 4e-11 divergence in the longest Gauss fit.
src/math had to be declared in src/lib.rs because the MATH domain root did not exist; that is the only edit outside this package's own files.
openmp: None. Neither the four .cpp files nor Eigen's NonLinearOptimization module carries a #pragma omp, so the port's serial execution matches the source's.
